**Finding submitted: compliant (at fallback).**

Section 4(a) gives AP a convenience-termination right on 90 days' notice after a one-year Initial Term, with no early-termination fee, and imposes the same 90-day notice discipline on Kubient. That satisfies the fallback on all three material terms:

| Material term | Playbook fallback | Clause 4(a) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer notice | 60–90 days | 90 days | Met |
| Early-termination fee | ≤ 3 months' fees | None (only fees *generated* in notice window) | Met |
| Vendor convenience notice | 90 days, end of term | 90 days, after Initial Term | Met |

Two gaps versus the *preferred* position were noted in the rationale rather than flagged, per the classification rules: Kubient's right runs at any point after the Initial Term rather than only at term-end, and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund. The refund gap is commercially immaterial here — Section 5 is a revenue share where Kubient remits auction proceeds to AP, so AP holds no prepaid fees to recover.

The one judgment call worth surfacing to the deal team: the "no termination during the Initial Term" lock-up would become a deviation if any Exhibit sets a longer initial term, since 4(a) expressly lets Exhibits vary termination rights. No Exhibits are attached to this document, so I assessed the MSA as drafted — worth a quick check when the Exhibits arrive.
